title: Optimize walkthrough - quantization profiles (INT8/FP8) - Aurora AI
summary: Redwood AE + SE walked Aurora AI through Redwood Optimize's quantization profile recommendations (INT8 vs FP8), presented quality vs latency tradeoffs using sample benchmarks, and agreed on pilot steps: share benchmark spreadsheet, run a short latency baseline on Aurora prompt set, and propose quant profiles for their top two models.
next_steps: Lena to share benchmark spreadsheet and sample quant profiles (link) by 2026-08-01
Marco to run 2-node latency baseline on Aurora sample (1k tokens) and share results by 2026-08-05
Sophie to upload prompt set and success criteria to the shared drive by 2026-07-31
action_items: Lena Park: Share benchmark spreadsheet and example quant profiles (INT8/FP8) - due 2026-08-01
Marco Ruiz: Run latency baseline on Aurora sample prompts (1k tokens) and upload results - due 2026-08-05
Sophie Chen: Provide prompt set and success criteria in shared folder - due 2026-07-31
transcript: Header:
Start time: 15:00 UTC
Duration: ~42 minutes
Attendees: Lena Park (Redwood AE), Marco Ruiz (Redwood SE), Sophie Chen (Aurora Head of ML), Dev Patel (Aurora Infra), Maya Singh (Aurora ML Eng)
Artifacts referenced: benchmark spreadsheet (https://redwood.app/benchmarks/aurora-quant), quant profiles doc (shared), security pack (sent via sales)

[00:00] Lena: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. Uh, we'll do a focused Optimize walkthrough today - quantization profiles, INT8 vs FP8, and a few quality vs latency comparisons. Marco will drive the bench examples.

[00:12] Sophie: Great, thanks. We're most interested in the latency gains at 1k and 4k token workloads, and where quality starts to degrade, so that's the most relevant thing for our chat bots and summarization pipelines.

[00:25] Marco: Yeah, perfect. Quick note on the setup - the numbers I'm going to show are from our internal profile runs on T4-style and A100-like instances; we did both an isolated latency SLO run and a throughput/batched run. There may be slight diffs when you run on your infra.
[00:40] Dev: Quick question - we're on GCP, N2D and A100 for heavy jobs. For a POC we'd likely spin up a dedicated pool. Does Redwood Optimize suggest different profiles for hosted vs dedicated?

[00:52] Marco: Good question. Short answer: yes. Hosted defaults favor FP8 when available because it gives a good quality/latency sweet spot for many open models, but for Dedicated with pinned kernels and custom quantized artifacts we sometimes push more aggressive INT8 for cost. We'll show examples.
[01:10] Maya: When you say "FP8 when available" - do you mean model-weight-format support or runtime support? We saw some variance across Hugging Face repos.

[01:20] Marco: It's both. FP8 requires model-aware kernel paths and in some cases a conversion step. Our Optimize tool picks the profile based on model family, sequence distribution, and your success criteria. The profile will say e.g., "INT8-8G-batched" vs "FP8-native-low-latency".
[01:38] Lena: I'll pause - Marco, can you share the first chart?

[01:42] Marco: Sure - pulling up the benchmark sheet. (brief share) Okay first chart: baseline full-precision (FP16/FP32) latency vs INT8 vs FP8 across a 1k token generation for the open-llm we used. You'll see latency drops ~30-45% INT8 and ~20-30% FP8 depending on kernel support.
[02:05] Sophie: Hmm that aligns with what we expected. What about quality? Do you have bleu/qa metrics or human evals?

[02:12] Marco: We ran a small automated quality check - ROUGE/BLEU-like and a model-specific instruction-following score. For the conversational prompts, INT8 had a ~1.8% drop on instruction score vs FP16, FP8 had ~0.7% drop. For summarization, INT8 was a bit noisier at longer sequences.
[02:33] Dev: Those %s are in your chart?
[02:35] Marco: Yup, included in the sheet (see column F/G). Note: results vary by model and prompt set; that's why we ask for your prompt set for an apples-to-apples POC.
[02:46] Maya: Are there memory/kv-cache differences? We're sensitive to working-set size - telling whether INT8 saves more RAM than FP8.

[02:54] Marco: INT8 generally reduces model memory footprint more - so you'll see some vRAM savings which can improve batching. FP8 is more about compute efficiency than maximum memory savings, though FP8 can still be smaller than FP16. Our optimizer recommends profiles with both memory and latency targets considered.

[03:10] Lena: I'll point out that Redwood Optimize also produces a candidate list - we give you 3 profiles per model: conservative (minimal quality loss), balanced (good latency with small quality delta), and aggressive (max speed/cost savings).
[03:23] Sophie: Good, we like the triage. Can you show an example profile for our Llama-variant?

[03:28] Marco: Yup - example: "balanced-llama2-13b-fp8" - target latency 180ms per 1k token, expected QA drop ~0.5% on our test set. The aggressive INT8 version pushes latency down to 120ms but QA drop goes up to 2%-3% in some instruction tasks.

[03:50] Sophie: OK. For our use-case, instruction fidelity is more important than 50ms gain, so we'd probably pick balanced or conservative for chat; aggressive might work for anonymized batch summarization.
[04:02] Dev: How deterministic are these numbers if we run on our A100s? Anything we should pin in the runtime?

[04:09] Marco: You should pin model version and quantization artifact. Also kernel versions - we recommend the kernel build we include in the POC repo. Without pinning you can see 5-10% variance in latency.
[04:20] Lena: Quick interruption - Sophie, can you confirm target latencies SLOs for chat?
[04:23] Sophie: We're aiming for p95 < 300ms at 1k tokens for chat, and cost target is to reduce per-token inference cost by at least 30% vs current infra.
[04:32] Lena: Perfect, that gives a clear objective. Marco, next chart?

[04:35] Marco: Next is quality vs latency curve across variants for 1k and 4k tokens. You'll notice for 4k sequences FP8 maintains quality better than INT8 in our evals - INT8 error accumulates at longer contexts.
[04:52] Maya: That makes sense - we've seen more decoding drift at longer sequences with aggressive quantization. Do you recommend mixed precision across layers?

[04:59] Marco: Yes, mixed precision is often the best compromise - keep critical layers (attention/query/key) at FP8/FP16 and apply INT8 to feedforward where tolerant. Our tooling can auto-generate a mixed profile for you.
[05:12] Sophie: How automated is that? We don't want to hand-tune layer by layer.
[05:16] Marco: It's automated. Optimize runs a sensitivity analysis and proposes the layer-level quant choices; we surface the results and you can approve the profile before rollout.
[05:25] Dev: For the POC, do we need to provide a specific CUDA/kernels image? We're running in a VPC private deployment for compliance.

[05:33] Lena: For Private deployments we provide an image and the conversion tool. If you're on Dedicated or Private, we can build a kernel image for your infra. We'll include an ops doc in the POC artifacts.
[05:44] Sophie: Security-wise we'll need to see encryption at rest and KMS integration. Also SOC2 and audit logs - is that in the pack?
[05:51] Lena: Yes - we'll attach the security pack. For Private, you control KMS; for Dedicated we integrate with customer KMS. We'll email the SOC2 summary and the audit log examples.

[05:59] Marco: Back to the results - here's a table showing cost per 1k tokens. INT8 aggressive can reduce unit cost by up to ~55% in some throughput workloads; balanced FP8 savings are more around 30-40%.
[06:12] Sophie: Curious - what's the impact on throughput when you enable prefix caching?

[06:16] Marco: Prefix/KV caching can drastically reduce cost for stateful chat. If your prompt set has long shared prefixes, effective per-token cost drops and the relative gains from quantization are additive. We can show sample runs in the POC.
[06:28] Maya: Are you able to run our exact workload? We have a mix of short chat replies and long summarize requests.
[06:34] Marco: Absolutely - that's why we asked for your prompt set. We'll run a mixed-workload baseline and then evaluate each profile against your success criteria.
[06:40] Lena: Quick pause - any vendor questions? Competitors?
[06:43] Sophie: We've also been talking to Anthropic and HF teams; they emphasize model-family-specific optimizations. How opinionated is Redwood Optimize vs manual tuning?

[06:53] Marco: Optimize is opinionated in that it recommends best-of models/profiles given constraints, but you can export the profiles and run manual tuning on top if desired. We often see customers accept the balanced recommendation and tweak one or two layers.
[07:05] Dev: On the logging and observability side, how do we tie quant-profile rollouts to our canary metrics?

[07:11] Marco: We provide per-request metadata for model/profile/version and Redwood Console surfaces cost/latency/quality deltas per-route. So you can set canary thresholds and automatic rollback on quality regression.
[07:22] Sophie: Nice. Walk me through a typical POC timeline - how long to a meaningful result?

[07:27] Lena: For the quantization and baseline runs we typically do a 2-3 week POC: week 1 gather assets and run baseline, week 2 run profiles and produce the report, week 3 iterate on the recommended profile and finalize ops checklist. If you want faster we can compress to 10 business days for a slimmed scope.
[07:42] Maya: Do you charge for the bench runs?

[07:45] Lena: We typically include one exploratory bench as part of the engagement; extended runs or dedicated capacity in the POC may be billable depending on scale - we'll capture that in the SOW / pricing doc.
[07:56] Marco: I'm going to demo one live run now - small prompt set (10 prompts) with Llama-variant. Running FP16 baseline... (pause, typing) p95 220ms, p50 120ms.
[08:15] Marco: Now applying balanced FP8 profile... (pause) p95 160ms, p50 90ms; automated quality check shows -0.6% on instruction score.
[08:30] Sophie: Do you have the raw outputs? I'd like to eyeball differences.
[08:33] Marco: Yep included in the sheet; here are two side-by-side generations - you'll see very minor token choice diffs mostly in punctuation and rarely instruction dropping.
[08:45] Dev: Any failure modes from quantizing - hallucinations or safety regressions?

[08:50] Marco: In our internal checks we look for safety and instruction-following regressions; severe regressions are uncommon with conservative or balanced profiles. Aggressive profiles increase the chance; that's why we recommend human review on those outputs during canary.
[09:04] Lena: OK quick check - are we aligned that Aurora wants to prioritize instruction fidelity for chat and can accept more aggressive profiles for batch summarization?
[09:12] Sophie: Yes, that's correct.
[09:14] Lena: Good. Next, looking at rollout patterns: canary on 5% traffic, then 20% then full - Redwood Console can automate that with automatic rollback if quality metric drops beyond threshold.
[09:28] Sophie: How do we instrument the quality metric? We run a small set of guarded prompts where we expect certain outputs.
[09:33] Marco: Exactly - Optimize supports prompt-set based evals and will run them on each profile. We'll tie the pass/fail to a canary policy.
[09:40] Maya: For the private deployment, does Redwood Optimize run in our VPC or is it a cloud-hosted service?

[09:45] Lena: Optimize can run in the private control plane for Private customers; the optimization engine needs telemetry and bench data but can be configured to only run on-prem if needed. We'll cover the architecture in the ops doc.
[09:57] Dev: That helps. About artifacts - can you send the quant profile format? We want to store it in our infra repo.
[10:02] Marco: We'll send the profile JSON/YAML; it includes model, layer map, quant params, and the recommended kernel image. I'll add an example to the shared folder.
[10:12] Sophie: Back to costs - you mentioned 30-55% savings. Do you have an example TCO calc?

[10:18] Marco: There is a sample TCO tab in the sheet where we project costs at 95% traffic and factor in caching benefits. For Aurora's mix of chat+batch, the conservative estimate is 28%-35% savings with balanced FP8.

[10:30] Lena: I'll note that Dedicated can give predictable throughput and sometimes better per-token economics if you're running sustained high QPS; we'll include both hosted and dedicated price comparisons in the proposal.
[10:40] Sophie: We may want to try Dedicated for the POC to simulate real load. Is there a minimum commit?
[10:45] Lena: There's a short-term Dedicated POC option; it's more an ops/setup conversation - I'll include the Dedicated POC options in the follow-up doc.

[10:53] Marco: Quick demo finish - I'll now show the mixed-precision profile generator: we upload your model, optimizer runs 45 sensitivity tests, and outputs three profiles and expected metrics - you can accept and export artifacts.
[11:10] Maya: That's neat. How invasive is the model conversion? Any retraining?

[11:15] Marco: No retraining. It's quantization-aware conversion and small calibration steps using a calibration corpus. For some models you can get further gains with a short quant-aware fine-tune, but it's optional.
[11:28] Dev: Calibration corpus - is that the prompt set we upload? Or do you need separate data?
[11:33] Marco: Preferably a small representative calibration set; it can be derived from your prompt set. We'll provide guidance on size (few hundred examples) and privacy handling.
[11:44] Sophie: On privacy, any data leaving our VPC in the POC?
[11:48] Lena: For Private deployments nothing leaves your VPC. For Hosted/demo runs we can do sampling or you can scrub data. We'll document options in the security pack.

[11:58] Marco: Moving toward wrap-up - I'll call out a couple of nuance items: 1) INT8 can require micro-kernel tuning per GPU generation, 2) FP8 adoption is growing but toolchains differ, 3) mixed profiles are usually the best practical outcome.
[12:17] Sophie: Noted. Anything else on the charts?
[12:20] Marco: One last chart - regression alerting: we show historical baseline and every deploy emits a diff; if ROUGE/instr drops beyond threshold we auto-create an incident in your on-call.
[12:32] Dev: Integration with our alerting (PagerDuty)?
[12:35] Marco: Yes PD and Slack integrations available.
[12:38] Lena: OK, let's summarize next steps and owners.

[12:42] Lena: Action items recap: Lena share bench sheet & profiles, Marco run baseline on Aurora sample, Sophie provide prompt set and success criteria. We'll schedule POC check-in on 2026-08-12. Any objections?
[12:55] Sophie: None, sounds good.
[12:58] Maya: One more small ask - can you include example export for CloudWatch metrics mapping?
[13:04] Marco: Yes, will include an example mapping file.
[13:08] Dev: And pricing?
[13:10] Lena: I'll send a draft pricing + Dedicated options after this call with the SOW and security pack.
[13:16] Sophie: Great. Thanks everyone - excited to see the POC results.
[13:20] Lena: Thanks all. We'll follow up via email with links. Bye
End of transcript (note: transcription contains some mis-hearings; speaker labels auto-generated).
